title: Test: Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards
summary: Check what you learned across the whole chapter.

questions.q: The section **Fallacies and Pitfalls** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: GRPO replaces the learned critic with G rollouts per task and broadcasts one standardized coefficient to every sampled token of a rollout, and its clipping and KL estimator choices change how that signal is weighted.
A terminal reward gives every turn the same reward-to-go, so separating a useful step from a faulty one is bought with a critic, more samples, or step-level signals, each at its own cost.
Agent RL throughput is set by the rollout loop, not the gradient step, so the serial slot cycle caps capacity and Amdahl's law bounds any single-stage speedup.
RLVR scores sampled rollouts with a programmatic check, so the update learns only what the sampler reaches and the reward distinguishes, and a task the policy never solves gives zero signal.

options: Grader isolation placed on the reward path protects the verdict from both the acting policy and the candidate code it submits, so a reward reflects executed tests rather than tampering.

questions.q: The section **Multi-Turn Agentic RL** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A group whose rewards all tie carries no reward gradient, occurring with probability p^G + (1-p)^G, so the rollout cost of one informative group is G/C and difficulty targeting toward p near 0.5 lowers it.
A terminal reward gives every turn the same reward-to-go, so separating a useful step from a faulty one is bought with a critic, more samples, or step-level signals, each at its own cost.
Ratios and gradients are valid only on per-invocation records of the delivered prefix token IDs, sampled token IDs, and behavior log probabilities under the actual sampling transforms.
Symmetric ratio clipping is asymmetric in probability space, so early successes sharpen the policy until groups converge and contrast vanishes, which outcome statistics can diagnose.
